extracted.intended_audience: actors, theatrical critics, and informed theatre-going public
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for judging stage acting and theatrical presentations (voice, physicality, emotional truth, fidelity to text, audience engagement, and critical integrity), illustrated by reviews of Edwin Forrest's performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for nature and good taste / avoid heterodox effects
rubrics_metrics.description: He disdained to overstep the prescribed bound for the sake of producing effects equally at variance with nature and heterodox to good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exaggerated or unnatural effects introduced solely for show; keep performance within believable, tasteful bounds. Antipattern: overacting that sacrifices naturalism for spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicious restraint and not overstrained execution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled, measured expression rather than forced intensity. Examples: subdued commands delivered as if not intended for the ear of the multitude were praised as judicious and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual emotional transitions / finely marked transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The gradual workings of his mind from calmness to jealousy were displayed with striking effect; the transitions of emotion ... were finely marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional changes should be built up progressively and clearly signaled; abrupt, unguided shifts are less effective. Scoring note: judges should value smooth, believable arcs between emotional states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal control and expressive tonal variation
rubrics_metrics.description: His voice then sank into tones the most touching, expressive of complaining regret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use changes in pitch, volume, and color to convey inner feeling (e.g., sinking to touching tones for regret). Antipattern: monotone delivery that flattens emotional nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness; avoid over-precision from obvious study
rubrics_metrics.description: The carefulness of his study is sometimes a little too obvious, giving an injurious hardness and over-precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough preparation is required but must not read as mechanical or overly 'studied.' Aim for studied truth rather than detectable technique. Penalize performances that feel rehearsed to the point of hardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verisimilitude / faithful realism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance should create a convincing reality onstage; gestures, voice, and behavior should feel authentic to character and situation. Example: portrayals that make the audience forget they are watching an actor are highly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid straining after effect; no grimacery
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no straining after effect,—there was no grimacery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on cheap effects, contortions, or affectations to elicit audience reaction. Natural expression is preferred to visible attempts to manipulate emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to rivet audience attention and engage sympathies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a test of an actor's skill that he is able to rivet the attention of the audience, and so to engage their thoughts and sympathies that they have not leisure even to applaud on the instant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong performance sustains audience focus and emotional involvement throughout; the measure is whether spectators remain absorbed rather than distracted or inclined to interrupt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained, whole performance — consistent excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Its great merit was that it was a whole, complete and finished. The spirit in which it began was equally sustained throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the performance as an integrated whole — consistency of conception, energy, and truth from opening to curtain are critical. Fluctuations in quality across acts reduce overall merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain dramatic illusion / preserve character on and off stage
rubrics_metrics.description: A striking proof of his sense of the propriety of keeping up the illusion ... He came on, preserving the same tottering gait which he had maintained throughout, and bowed his thanks as much in the guise of Lear as he had acted in the drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors should preserve the character's demeanor even during bows or curtain calls when it serves the illusion; sudden breaks can dissipate the dramatic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delicate shading and subtle variations of emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Slight changes in emphasis, tone, or action, delicate shadings and pencillings, are observed with singular and most gratifying quickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nuance and micro-choices in delivery are prized; small alterations in emphasis or gesture can convey deep character information and are noticed by informed audiences. Encourage subtlety over broad strokes when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for conventional 'correct' readings (textual fidelity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variations from the accustomed modes, though not in any palpable new readings,—which, for the most part, are bad readings, for there is generally but one mode positively correct, and that has not been left for us to discover,—
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While tasteful nuance is welcome, wholesale new readings of canonical passages are risky; many critics value established, textually faithful interpretations. Antipattern: radical reinterpretations that conflict with the text's evident meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical accuracy in characterization (age, infirmity, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The great accuracy and fidelity with which the decrepitude of the aged monarch was portrayed ... The palsied head and quivering limbs were so correctly given ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical choices (gait, posture, tremors) must be accurate and consistent with the character's condition; attention to physical detail enhances believability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tasteful originality and 'fine touch' true to scene and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: He introduced a new and a very striking point ... This fine touch, so true to the scene and to nature, drew down several rounds of applause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original interpretive choices are welcome when they arise naturally from the scene and character; novelty should serve truth rather than shock. Reward clever, tasteful innovations that illuminate the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain climactic intensity without collapse into tameness
rubrics_metrics.description: The difficulty is for an actor so to manage his powers as to give full effect to the whole, without sinking into apparent tameness in the last imprecation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage pacing and energy to build through to climactic moments; failure to sustain intensity at critical points weakens the effect. Assessors should note whether power is maintained to the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match delivery to psychological truth of the line (tone and force)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Macbeth ... the passage ought to be uttered as the proud boast of one who was confident of supernatural protection, and not in a taunting, sneering manner ... 'Had I but died an hour before this chance, I had lived a blessed time,'—was delivered with most inappropriate calmness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery must align with the speaker's psychological state and context; evaluate whether tone, volume, and inflection convey the intended inner life (e.g., boastfulness, remorse, horror). Examples from Macbeth indicate specific mismatches to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity over trickery; avoid being labeled a quack
rubrics_metrics.description: We had also seen quite enough of Mr. Forrest to convince us that he is a man of real talent, with very little, if any, mere trickery in his acting, so that to stigmatize him as a quack or an impostor was ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine craft and depth are preferable to surface tricks or gimmicks. Critics should distinguish authentic talent from manipulative showmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate energy/power — avoid being too subdued or too colloquial
rubrics_metrics.description: There was, however, in many parts of his performance a lack of power. Mr. Forrest was too subdued,—too colloquial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performances must calibrate energy to role and moment: not every passage should be restrained; some require higher pitch and emphasis. Penalize underpowered or inappropriately casual deliveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing that yields seasonable applause and shows textual comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: They applaud warmly, but seasonably. They do not interrupt a passion ... They applaud in the intervals of the dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-paced acting allows audience reactions to occur at appropriate moments, preserving dramatic flow; indications of textual comprehension by the audience (timely applause) reflect effective pacing and clarity.
